;Business and economy
*The [[Government of the Islamic Republic of Iran|Iranian government]] announces that, effective immediately, [[Gasoline | petrol]] will be rationed to 60 litres per month, and prices will increase 50%. Fuel beyond the limit will cost double. Iranians take to the streets to oppose the plan, which results from [[United States sanctions against Iran]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/ajimpact/petrol-rationing-price-hikes-iranians-surprise-191115155053008.html (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/11/15/world/middleeast/iran-gasoline-prices-rations.html (''The New York Times'')]

;International relations
*[[North Korean abductions of Japanese citizens]], [[Japan–North Korea relations]]
**[[Yokota family|Sakie Yokota]], the mother of a [[Japanese people|Japanese]] girl abducted by [[North Korea]] 42 years ago at the age of 13, appeals directly to [[Kim Jong-un]] to release her and all Japanese abductees. She also decries the lack of [[Japanese government]] action on the issue. [https://www3.nhk.or.jp/nhkworld/en/news/20191115_17/ (NHK World-Japan)]
*[[Japan–South Korea relations]], [[Japan–United States relations]], [[South Korea–United States relations]]
**Japan, [[South Korea]] and the [[United States]] agree to boost multilateral military cooperation and defense issues. [https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20191115004300325 (Yonhap News Agency)]

;Law and crime
*[[Criminal charges brought in the Mueller special counsel investigation]]
**A federal jury convicts [[Roger Stone]] of lying to the [[United States Congress]] and tampering with a witness about his efforts to learn about the anti-secrecy group [[WikiLeaks]]'s release of [[2016 Democratic National Committee email leak|hacked Democratic emails]] in the [[2016 United States elections|2016 U.S. presidential election]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/local/public-safety/roger-stone-jury-weighs-evidence-and-a-defense-move-to-make-case-about-mueller/2019/11/15/554fff5a-06ff-11ea-8292-c46ee8cb3dce_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Hong Kong protests]]
**A 70-year-old bystander dies after being hit by a brick while filming a clash between protesters and residents. Police is treating the act as a murder. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-50428704 (BBC News)] [https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/politics/article/3037927/hong-kong-protests-police-treat-death-70-year-old-cleaner (''South China Morning Post'')]
**[[Pro-Beijing]] Hong Kong Justice Secretary [[Teresa Cheng (politician)|Teresa Cheng]] suffers minor injuries after being heckled in [[London]]. China's Foreign Ministry condemns the protesters. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-hongkong-protests-diplomacy/china-strongly-condemns-attack-on-hong-kong-government-official-in-london-idUSKBN1XP0BM?il=0 (Reuters)] [https://www.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3037830/hong-kong-justice-secretary-teresa-cheng-injured-london-while (''South China Morning Post'')]
*[[2019 Chilean protests]]
**An agreement is signed by most of the political parties supporting a referendum in April 2020 regarding the draft of a new constitution through a [[Constituent assembly|constituent convention]]. This will be the first time the Constitution of Chile is written with popular participation. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/nov/15/chile-referendum-new-constitution-protests (''The Guardian'')]

*[[2019 Bolivian protests]]
**Security forces open fire on protesters in [[Cochabamba]], killing at least five. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/bolivia-protests-deaths-1.5362104 (CBC News)]
